dossier.public_summary: The dip is not repeatable: three deep events dominate the score while most transits vanish, and the depth changes dramatically from sector to sector even in the same TESS pipeline. The target is a rapidly spotted star at a stellar rotation period near half the claimed period, so the signal looks like uncorrected variability or a nearby blend rather than a 1.5-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Signal is driven by 3 extreme outliers (1674, 1654, 1663 ppm) that carry 88% of the signal; many transits are undetected or negative (-249, -155 ppm). Not multiple consistent transits.

Depth is not stable: 1328 ppm in sector 20 and 892 ppm in sector 44 with uncertainties 93,125 ppm, but 38 ppm in sector 60, -17 ppm in sector 71, -65 ppm in sector 72 within same pipeline. Consistent with blend systematics/Crowdsaps, not a steady planet.

Star is a highly spotted variable (5040-17171 ppm modulation) with 2:1 period commensurability to the 12.2-d dip. Spot/instrument systematics plausibly generate the shallow, spot-correlated dips instead of a transit.
